other_failure_modes.name: Data Leakage in Cross-Validation
other_failure_modes.description: Feature engineering steps such as frequency encoding, spatial K-Means clustering, and median imputation are fitted on the entire training dataset before it is split into cross-validation folds. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the out-of-fold validation scores overly optimistic and potentially causing suboptimal model selection or ensemble weight computation.

summary: The agent implements a strong and robust solution with extensive feature engineering, multiple models (LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and a custom TabularResNet), and an optimized ensemble. The primary flaw is data leakage during cross-validation, as several feature engineering steps (K-Means clustering, frequency encoding, and imputation) are fit on the entire training dataset before splitting into folds. The code avoids major data science failure modes and correctly protects the held-out test set.
